classification.difficultyReason: Use midpoint equality, equate two routes to each endpoint, and substitute the resulting expressions into the scaffolded identity.

content.prompt:
$M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of $AB$ and $PQ$.

Let $\underset{\sim}{u}=\overrightarrow{AM}$, $\underset{\sim}{v}=\overrightarrow{PN}$, $\underset{\sim}{a}=\overrightarrow{AP}$, $\underset{\sim}{b}=\overrightarrow{BQ}$ and $\underset{\sim}{p}=\overrightarrow{MN}$.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral ABQP with midpoint segment MN; all six labels and no arrows or ticks.
spec.mathematics: M is the midpoint of AB and N is the midpoint of PQ. AP, MN and BQ are horizontal in the source illustration; no additional parallelism is asserted.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{AM}$ and $\overrightarrow{MB}$ have the same length and direction. Similarly, $\overrightarrow{PN}$ and $\overrightarrow{NQ}$ have the same length and direction.
answer.worked: Since $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, $\overrightarrow{AM}$ and $\overrightarrow{MB}$ have the same length and direction, so $\overrightarrow{MB}=\underset{\sim}{u}$. Similarly, since $N$ is the midpoint of $PQ$, $\overrightarrow{PN}$ and $\overrightarrow{NQ}$ have the same length and direction, so $\overrightarrow{NQ}=\underset{\sim}{v}$.
